name: Serralves Foundation
short: Serralves contemporary art foundation: Álvaro Siza Vieira's museum (1999) and an Art Deco villa in an 18-hectare park.
long: Serralves is a cultural complex in Porto bringing together a contemporary art museum, a park and a villa, each representing a different era: contemporary architecture, modernism and Art Deco. The museum building was designed by Álvaro Siza Vieira and opened on 6 June 1999. Casa de Serralves, built between 1925 and 1944 for Carlos Alberto Cabral, is a leading example of Art Deco in Portugal. The roughly 18-hectare park holds a collection of open-air sculptures.
history:
In December 1986 the State acquired the Serralves estate in order to house the future National Museum of Modern Art. The park and villa opened to the public on 29 May 1987.

On 27 July 1989 a decree established the Serralves Foundation, an innovative partnership between the State and civil society. In March 1991 the foundation signed a contract with the architect Álvaro Siza Vieira to design the museum.

The museum was built on the estate's former vegetable gardens and opened on 6 June 1999. The 13,000-square-metre building includes 4,500 square metres of exhibition space in 14 galleries; an auditorium was added in 2000.

Casa de Serralves was built by Carlos Alberto Cabral, 2nd Count of Vizela, to a design by José Marques da Silva. Its interior decoration is linked to names such as Ruhlmann, Lalique, Brandt and Perzel; the villa was built between 1925 and 1944.

The museum's collection begins at 1968; there is no permanent display, but around five exhibitions by invited artists are staged each year. In 2012 the whole complex was classified as a national monument of Portugal.
facts: The museum building was designed by Álvaro Siza Vieira and opened on 6 June 1999.
Casa de Serralves is an Art Deco villa built between 1925 and 1944 to a design by José Marques da Silva.
The park covers about 18 hectares and won the Henry Ford Environment Prize in 1997.
The museum covers 13,000 square metres, with 4,500 square metres of exhibition space in 14 galleries.
The collection focuses on art made after 1968; there is no permanent exhibition.
The park displays works by Richard Serra, Dan Graham and Claes Oldenburg.
In 2012 the complex was classified as a national monument of Portugal.
tip: The ticket covers both the museum and the park, so allow at least half a day. You can reach it by bus to Avenida Marechal Gomes da Costa; check current hours and concessions at serralves.pt.
